verses.zh: 巴比伦的处女啊，下来坐在尘埃；迦勒底的闺女啊，没有宝座，要坐在地上；因为你不再称为柔弱娇嫩的。
verses.en: “Fall down! Sit in the dirt,O virgin[NOTE:1] daughter Babylon!Sit on the ground, not on a throne,O daughter of the Babylonians!Indeed,[NOTE:2] you will no longer be called delicate and pampered.
notes: בְּתוּלַה (betulah) often refers to a virgin, but the phrase “virgin daughter” is apparently stylized (see also 23:12; 37:22). In the extended metaphor of this chapter, where Babylon is personified as a queen (vv. 5, 7), she is depicted as being both a wife and mother (vv. 8-9).
Or “For” (NASB, NRSV).
verses.commentary:
47:1 "Come down" This funeral dirge is one of three literary models used by the Hebrew
prophets to communicate their divine messages.

- funeral dirge

- court scene

- promise oracle

▣ "sit in the dust" See SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES

▣ "O virgin daughter of Babylon" This was a Semitic idiom of security and
preciousness in family imagery. She (the Neo-Babylonian Empire) who was so secure and
protected, has now become vulnerable.

▣ "sit in the dust. . .sit on the ground without a throne" This is literally "sit"
(BDB 442, KB 444, Qal IMPERATIVE, cf. Isa. 47:1 [twice],5,8 [twice]). It was
one of the physical signs of mourning.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES

▣ "O daughter of the Chaldeans" This is parallel to "Babylon," see full note at Isa. 43:14. It
is repeated in v. 5.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHALDEANS

▣ "shall no longer be called tender and delicate" These two terms (BDB 940 and 772)
are used in Deut. 28:56 for luxurious, extravagant living. This is contrasted with Isa. 47:2-3, where she is now

- a slave

- a prostitute

verses.zh: 要用磨磨面，揭去帕子，脱去长衣，露腿蹚河。
verses.en: Pick up millstones and grind flour.Remove your veil,strip off your skirt,expose your legs,cross the streams.
verses.commentary:
47:2-3 This is a series of phrases used to describe one who used to be the queen of the nations
(Isa. 47:5,7) and is now a slave.

- she grinds meal, Isa. 47:2

- she removes her veil, Isa. 47:2

- she had to prepare her clothes for hard labor, Isa. 47:2

- she had to cross the rivers herself and not be carried (possibly into exile), Isa. 47:2

- her nakedness was uncovered, Isa. 47:3 (cf. Jer. 13:26)

- as a punishment for sin (cf. Isa. 20:4)

- simply the lot of slaves who were poorly clad and sexually vulnerable

verses.zh: 你的下体必被露出；你的丑陋必被看见。我要报仇，谁也不宽容。
verses.en: Let your naked body be exposed.Your shame will be on display![NOTE:1] I will get revenge;I will not have pity on anyone,”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb In this context “shame” is a euphemism referring to their naked bodies.
Heb “I will not meet a man.” The verb פָּגַע (paga‘) apparently carries the nuance “meet with kindness” here (cf. 64:5, and see BDB 803 s.v. Qal.2).
verses.commentary:
47:3

NASB
"and will not spare a man"

NKJV
"I will not arbitrate with a man"

NRSV
"I will spare no one"

TEV
"no one will stop me"

NJB
"no one stands in My way"

REB
"show clemency to none"

JPSOA
"let no man intercede"

LXX
"I will no longer deliver you over to men"

Peshitta
"I will not meet you as a man"

This is a somewhat ambiguous phrase but the VERB "I will not spare" (BDB 803, KB 910, Qal
IMPERFECT), had an etymological relationship to prayerful intercession (BDB 803, KB 910,
cf. Isa. 53:12; 59:16; Jer. 36:25). It seems to mean that no one could intercede for Neo-Babylon or that no human
was powerful enough in prayer to stop YHWH's predetermined plan for her judgment.

verses.zh: 我们救赎主的名是万军之耶和华―以色列的圣者。
verses.en: says our Protector—the Lord of Heaven’s Armies is his name,the Holy One of Israel.[NOTE:1]
notes: See the note on the phrase “the Holy One of Israel” in 1:4.tc The Hebrew text reads, “Our redeemer—the Lord of armies [traditionally, “the Lord of hosts”] is his name, the Holy One of Israel.” The ancient Greek version adds “says” before “our redeemer.” אָמַר (ʾamar) may have accidentally dropped from the text by virtual haplography. Note that the preceding word אָדָם (ʾadam) is graphically similar.
verses.commentary:
47:4 This is an exclamation from the author who interjects himself into the flow of poetry (REB adds "says" to
the MT, making these statements come from YHWH. The UBS Text Project, p. 127, gives this option a "B" rating). Three
of the beautiful titles for God are seen here as the prophet praises YHWH for Who He is. The titles are:

- Redeemer ‒ an emphasis on God as Savior; He is the One who buys people back from
slavery (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM)

- Lord of hosts ‒ a Persian title which focuses on one of two areas (see

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS)

- the angelic council, Isa. 24:21-22 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVENLY COUNCIL OF ANGELIC BEINGS)

- the astral deities of Babylon, Isa. 40:26

- the Holy One of Israel ‒ the title for God who will bring this to pass on behalf of
His people (see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE)

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

verses.zh: 迦勒底的闺女啊，你要默然静坐，进入暗中，因为你不再称为列国的主母。
verses.en: “Sit silently! Go to a hiding place,[NOTE:1] O daughter of the Babylonians!Indeed,[NOTE:2] you will no longer be called ‘Queen of kingdoms.’
notes: Heb “darkness,” which may indicate a place of hiding where a fugitive would seek shelter and protection.
Or “For” (NASB, NRSV).
verses.commentary:
47:5 "Sit silently, and go into darkness" This major world power has now become a peasant. This
verse tells her to seek obscurity and be silent (two IMPERATIVES).

▣ "The queen of kingdoms" This is an idiom of Neo-Babylon's view of itself and its
power (cf. Isa. 47:7). The queen has become a sex slave (cf. Isa. 47:2-3,8a). What she did to exiles will
now happen to her (i.e. divinely caused role reversal).

It is just possible that this idiom relates to Nabonidus leading Neo-Babylon away from
Marduk to the worship of the moon goddess called "the Queen of heaven." She was called Sin
(Akkadian) or Nanna (Sumerian).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOON WORSHIP

verses.zh: 我向我的百姓发怒，使我的产业被亵渎，将他们交在你手中，你毫不怜悯他们，把极重的轭加在老年人身上。
verses.en: I was angry at my people;I defiled my special possessionand handed them over to you.You showed them no mercy;[NOTE:1] you even placed a very heavy burden on old people.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “compassion.”
Heb “on the old you made very heavy your yoke.”
verses.commentary:
47:6 "I was angry with My people" This explains why the covenant people were taken into
exile. In the ancient world the deity of the individual nations protected them. The fact that both Israel
and Judah were taken captive was seen by the ANE world as the gods of the Fertile Crescent being more
powerful than the God of Israel, but this was not the case. God was using the powers of the Fertile
Crescent to judge His people for their sin (cf. Isa. 10:5; 42:24). This was clearly foreshadowed in Lev. 26 and Deut. 28.

▣ "You did not show mercy on them" Although God gave His people to Assyria and
Babylon in order to punish them, these pagan nations went too far and now they will be judged for
their lack of mercy.

verses.zh: 你自己说：我必永为主母，所以你不将这事放在心上，也不思想这事的结局。
verses.en: You said,‘I will rule forever as permanent queen!’[NOTE:1] You did not think about these things;[NOTE:2] you did not consider how it would turn out.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Forever I [will be] permanent queen”; NIV “the eternal queen”; CEV “queen forever.”
Heb “you did not set these things upon your heart [or “mind”].”
Heb “you did not remember its outcome”; NAB “you disregarded their outcome.”
verses.commentary:
47:7 "These things you did not consider

Nor remember the outcome of them"

The two VERBS are Qal PERFECTS, which
denote a settled attitude.

- did not consider, lit. "did not lay these things to heart"

- did not remember their end

Notice how Isa. 47:8 continues the thought.

verses.zh: 你这专好宴乐、安然居住的，现在当听这话。你心中说：惟有我，除我以外再没有别的。我必不致寡居，也不遭丧子之事。
verses.en: So now, listen to this,O one who lives so lavishly,[NOTE:1] who lives securely,who says to herself,[NOTE:2] ‘I am unique! No one can compare to me![NOTE:3] I will never have to live as a widow;I will never lose my children.’[NOTE:4]
notes: Or perhaps, “voluptuous one” (NAB); NAB “you sensual one”; NLT “You are a pleasure-crazy kingdom.”
Heb “the one who says in her heart.”
Heb “I [am], and besides me there is no other.” See Zeph 2:15.
Heb “I will not live [as] a widow, and I will not know loss of children.”
verses.commentary:
47:8-9 "Who dwells securely. . .but these two things shall come upon you suddenly" It seems
from Daniel 5 and from Herodotus that the people of Neo-Babylon laughed at the approaching Persian army.
However, the Persian army rechanneled the waters of the Euphrates River, went under the walls of this
magnificent city, and in one day the city fell (cf. Daniel 5). The common people of the city of Babylon saw
the Persians as liberators because Belshazzar and his father, Nabonidus, had begun to worship a strange
moon goddess called Sin (Nanna, see
SPECIAL TOPIC: MOON WORSHIP) and Cyrus II allowed them to return to their traditional
deities—Bel, Marduk, and Nebo.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MARDUK

SPECIAL TOPIC: NEBO

47:8

NASB
"sensual one"

NKJV, Peshitta
"you who are given to pleasure"

REB
"lover of luxury"

JPSOA
"pampered one"

NJB
"voluptuous woman"

TEV, NRSV
"lover of pleasure"

LXX
"luxurious one"

This is a rare Hebrew ADJECTIVE (BDB 726, KB 792) which denotes
one accustomed to an easy, pampered life.

▣ "I am, and there is no one beside me" This is an obvious challenge to the uniqueness of
YHWH (cf. Isa. 47:10; same language used by Nineveh in Zeph. 2:5). Which One delivered His people? Which
One is the true, unique God who possesses power?

verses.zh: 哪知，丧子、寡居这两件事在一日转眼之间必临到你；正在你多行邪术、广施符咒的时候，这两件事必全然临到你身上。
verses.en: Both of these will come upon yousuddenly, in one day!You will lose your children and be widowed.[NOTE:1] You will be overwhelmed by these tragedies,[NOTE:2] despite[NOTE:3] your many incantationsand your numerous amulets.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “loss of children and widowhood.” In the Hebrew text the phrase is in apposition to “both of these” in line 1.
Heb “according to their fullness, they will come upon you.”
For other examples of the preposition bet (בְּ) having the sense of “although, despite,” see BDB 90 s.v. III.7.
Reference is made to incantations and amulets, both of which were important in Mesopotamian religion. They were used to ward off danger and demons.
verses.commentary:
47:9 "Loss of children" Note Isa. 13:16,18. What she did to others will happen to her!

▣ "many sorceries. . .the great power of your spells" The emphasis on Neo-Babylon's
occultic practices, made so specific here, is continued in Isa. 47:11-13. These practices are
condemned in Deuteronomy 18. For all her magical arts Neo-Babylon could not protect herself, which
shows the ineffectiveness of occult practices (i.e. the weakness of her gods).

- sorceries ‒ BDB 506

- spells ‒ BDB 288 I

The NET Bible, p. 1260, #23, thinks these terms refer to spells and amulets that were
worn by most people in the ANE to ward off evil spells, demons, bad luck, or danger.

See a good brief discussion in IVP Bible Background Commentary (OT), p. 631.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MAGIC

verses.zh: 你素来倚仗自己的恶行，说：无人看见我。你的智慧聪明使你偏邪，并且你心里说：惟有我，除我以外再没有别的。
verses.en: You were complacent in your evil deeds;[NOTE:1] you thought,[NOTE:2] ‘No one sees me.’Your self-professed[NOTE:3] wisdom and knowledge lead you astray,when you say, ‘I am unique! No one can compare to me!’[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “you trusted in your evil”; KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV “wickedness.”
Or “said”; NAB “said to yourself”’ NASB “said in your heart.”
The words “self-professed” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
See the note at v. 8.
verses.commentary:
47:10 "secure in your wickedness" The Dead Sea Scrolls change "wickedness" (BDB 949)
by changing a "d" to an "r," which makes it mean "knowledge" (BDB 395, which occurs in line c of v. 10).
Either of these words fits the context.

▣ "No one sees me" This implies that they knew what they were doing was wicked
and were trying to hide themselves (cf. Isa. 29:15).

verses.zh: 因此，祸患要临到你身，你不知何时发现（或译：如何驱逐）；灾害落在你身上，你也不能除掉；所不知道的毁灭也必忽然临到你身。
verses.en: Disaster will overtake you;you will not know how to charm it away.[NOTE:1] Destruction will fall on you;you will not be able to appease it.Calamity will strike you suddenly,before you recognize it.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew text has שַׁחְרָהּ (shakhrah), which is either a suffixed noun (“its dawning,” i.e., origin) or infinitive (“to look early for it”). Some have suggested an emendation to שַׁחֲדָהּ (shakhadah), a suffixed infinitive from שָׁחַד (shakhad, “[how] to buy it off”; see BDB 1005 s.v. שָׁחַד). This forms a nice parallel with the following couplet. The above translation is based on a different etymology of the verb in question. HALOT 1466 s.v. III שׁחר references a verbal root with these letters (שׁחד) that refers to magical activity.
Heb “you will not know”; NIV “you cannot foresee.”
verses.commentary:
47:11

NASB, NRSV, NJB, JPSOA, NET
"charm away"

NKJV, Peshitta
"from where it arises"

TEV
"your magic can not stop it"

JPSOA footnote
"bribe"

REB
"conjure it away"

The MT, "you cannot know her dawn," thus the Peshitta and NKJV translations. There
have been several suggested emendations.

- from the root (KB 1466 III) "to cause to disappear by magic," thus NASB, REB, NET trandslations

- from a root (JPSOA footnote) "to bribe" or "buy off," from BDB 1005

▣ "atone" This is the Hebrew word "to cover" (BDB 497, KB 493, Piel INFINITIVE
CONSTRUCT) and is used of the OT concept of
atonement as being a blood covering on the mercy seat (cf. Leviticus 16).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ATONEMENT

▣ "suddenly" This certainly describes the fall of the city of Babylon.

verses.zh: 站起来吧！用你从幼年劳神施行的符咒和你许多的邪术；或者可得益处，或者可得强胜。
verses.en: Persist[NOTE:1] in trusting[NOTE:2] your amuletsand your many incantations,which you have faithfully recited[NOTE:3] since your youth!Maybe you will be successful[NOTE:4]—maybe you will scare away disaster.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “stand” (so KJV, ASV); NASB, NRSV “Stand fast.”
The word “trusting” is supplied in the translation for clarification. See v. 9.
Heb “in that which you have toiled.”
Heb “maybe you will be able to profit.”
Heb “maybe you will cause to tremble.” The object “disaster” is supplied in the translation for clarification. See the note at v. 9.
verses.commentary:
47:12 "Perhaps you may cause trembling" H. C. Leupold adds the word "me" to show the possibility
that God is telling them to see if their spells threaten Him or cause Him to tremble. This seems to be the
meaning of the passage. It may, however, refer to the Persian army (NJB).

verses.zh: 你筹划太多，以致疲倦。让那些观天象的，看星宿的，在月朔说预言的，都站起来，救你脱离所要临到你的事。
verses.en: You are tired out from listening to so much advice.[NOTE:1] Let them take their stand—the ones who see omens in the sky,who gaze at the stars,who make monthly predictions—let them rescue you from the disaster that is about to overtake you![NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “you are tired because of the abundance of your advice.”
Heb “let them stand and rescue you—the ones who see omens in the sky, who gaze at the stars, who make known by months—from those things which are coming upon you.”
verses.commentary:
47:13 Not only are Neo-Babylon's deities helpless and humiliated (cf. Isa. 47:1-3,5), but also her
prophets and counselors/sorcerers (cf. Isa. 47:14).

▣

NASB, NKJV, LXX
"counsels"

NRSV, NJB
"consultations"

TEV
"advise"

JPSOA
"art"

This is the same Hebrew word, "counsel" (BDB 420 calls it "political consultation")
that is translated "purpose" (REB) in Isa. 46:10,11. This may be a contrast between YHWH's plans/purposes
that will come to pass and the faulty, weak, ineffective plans/purposes of the Neo-Babylonian religious elite!

No one "counseled" YHWH (cf. Isa. 40:13). He always fulfills His plans (cf. Isa. 44:26; 46:10,11).

▣

NASB, NKJV, TEV, NJB, LXX
"astrologers"

NRSV
"those who study the heavens"

JPSOA
"scanners of heavens"

Peshitta
"Chaldeans"

Emphasized Bible
"the dividers of the heavens"

The MT has the Qal PERFECT of BDB 211, KB 237
(ketiv), which seems to mean "to divide" from an Arabic root. The Masoretic scholars
suggested that the Qal PARTICIPLE of the same root be read (qere). If
this is accurate then it is parallel with "those who prophesy by the stars" (i.e. astrologers).

verses.zh: 他们要像碎秸被火焚烧，不能救自己脱离火焰之力；这火并非可烤的炭火，也不是可以坐在其前的火。
verses.en: Look, they are like strawthat the fire burns up;they cannot rescue themselvesfrom the heat[NOTE:1] of the flames.There are no coals to warm them,no firelight to enjoy.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “hand,” here a metaphor for the strength or power of the flames.

The Hebrew text reads literally, “there is no coal [for?] their food, light to sit before it.” Some emend לַחְמָם (lakhmam, “their food”) to לְחֻמָּם (lekhummam, “to warm them”; see HALOT 328 s.v. חמם). This statement may allude to Isa 44:16, where idolaters are depicted warming themselves over a fire made from wood, part of which was used to form idols. The fire of divine judgment will be no such campfire; its flames will devour and destroy.
verses.commentary:
47:14 Verse 14 has one unified theme (i.e. judgment by fire) or the first three lines are
judgment but the last two may relate to astrologers, the false prophets or enchanters finding a place
of comfort from the cold weather by the fire they made from the scraps of their wooden idols (i.e. Isa. 44:16).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible
for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy
Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this
section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- What is the play between Isa. 45:23 and 46:1-2?

- What is the word play between Isa. 46:1-2 and 46:3-4?

- List the number of ways that monotheism is emphasized in Isaiah 46 and 47.

- What does 46:8 have in common with Isa. 46:12?

- How does one reconcile God's control over history and human freedom?

- Why is Isa. 46:12-13 important to our concept of justification by faith?

- List the number of ways that Babylon has fallen from luxury to slavery.

- List the types of occult practices found in Isa. 47:9-13.

verses.zh: 你所劳神的事都要这样与你无益；从幼年与你贸易的也都各奔各乡，无人救你。
verses.en: They will disappoint you,[NOTE:1] those you have so faithfully dealt with since your youth.[NOTE:2] Each strays off in his own direction,[NOTE:3] leaving no one to rescue you.”
notes: Heb “So they will be to you”; NIV84 “That is all they can do for you”; NIV11 “That is all they are to you.”
Heb “that for which you toiled, your traders from your youth.” The omen readers and star gazers are likened to merchants with whom Babylon has had an ongoing economic relationship.
Heb “each to his own side, they err.”

"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- If chapter 46 emphasized the fall of the Neo-Babylonian idols, then chapter 47 describes the
fall of the empire itself (i.e. the city of Babylon) along with its occult prophets and priests.

- Verses 1-7 have a series of IMPERATIVES directed at Neo-Babylon, depicted as a prostitute/queen.

- come down, Isa. 47:1 ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 432, KB 434)

- sit in the dust, Isa. 47:1 ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 442, KB 444)

- sit on the ground, Isa. 47:1 ‒ same as #2 (notice the number of times this term is
used in Isa. 47:1 [twice],5, 8 [twice])

- take, Isa. 47:2 ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 542, KB 534)

- grind, Isa. 47:2 ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 377, KB 374)

- remove your veil, Isa. 47:2 ‒ Piel IMPERATIVE (BDB 162, KB 191)

- strip off the skirt, Isa. 47:2 ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 362, KB 359)

- uncover the leg, Isa. 47:2 ‒ Piel IMPERATIVE (BDB 162, KB 191)

- cross the river, Isa. 47:2 ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 716, KB 778)

- let your nakedness be uncovered, Isa. 47:3 ‒ Niphal JUSSIVE (BDB 162, KB 191)

- sit silently, Isa. 47:5 ‒ same as #3,4

- go into darkness, Isa. 47:5 ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 97, KB 112)

- The prophetic literary form of this chapter is a "funeral dirge." It is recognized by its unique
beat/meter in Hebrew (3, 2 beat, like the poems of Lamentations). It is a funeral lament but in a
sarcastic sense (Taunt Song).

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ISAIAH 47:1-7

1"Come down and sit in the dust,

O virgin daughter of Babylon;

Sit on the ground without a throne,

O daughter of the Chaldeans!

For you shall no longer be called tender and delicate.

2Take the millstones and grind meal.

Remove your veil, strip off the skirt,

Uncover the leg, cross the rivers.

3Your nakedness will be uncovered,

Your shame also will be exposed;

I will take vengeance and will not spare a man."

4Our Redeemer, the Lord of hosts is His name,

The Holy One of Israel.

5"Sit silently, and go into darkness,

O daughter of the Chaldeans,

For you will no longer be called

The queen of kingdoms.

6I was angry with My people,

I profaned My heritage

And gave them into your hand.

You did not show mercy to them,

On the aged you made your yoke very heavy.

7Yet you said, 'I will be a queen forever.'

These things you did not consider

Nor remember the outcome of them.
